data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["Biological species evolve naturally via mutation; software stacks are chosen via procurement and standardization."],"overturn_conditions":["If the 'colony' shares a single critical biological vulnerability (e.g., a specific receptor), the analogy fails."],"shared_structure":["Comparison between a specialized organism (centralized) and a multi-species colony (decentralized).","Trade-off between internal regulation and environmental robustness."],"source_memory_refs":["SCR_001"],"transfer_claims":["Systemic resilience is derived from heterogeneity rather than the volume of redundancy."]},"claim":"A decentralized network is more resilient to correlated failure only if its 'Diversity Index' exceeds the 'Coupling Coefficient' of the centralized service's control plane.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The decentralized services converge on a single industry-standard dependency (e.g., a specific version of OpenSSL) that introduces a shared vulnerability.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The cost of coordination in the decentralized network leads to a consensus collapse during a crisis, creating a systemic failure absent in centralized systems.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Resilience is not a function of scale or redundancy, but of the overlap in the dependency trees (OS, kernel, libraries, cloud providers) across the system. A decentralized network reduces correlation by distributing these dependencies across different operators, whereas a large service\u2014even with high redundancy\u2014often shares a singular, monolithic control plane or a standardized internal library set that creates a single point of failure (Common Mode Failure).","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
